title: Jacobians of abelian Cayley digraphs: quantitative bounds and a full proof of BKR Proposition 6.19
statement: Let A be a finite abelian group of order n >= 2 and S a multiset of nonzero elements of A with sum 0 that generates A. Then the Jacobian of the Cayley digraph Cay(A, S) is isomorphic to A if and only if A is cyclic and S = {a, -a} for a generator a. More precisely |Jac| > n whenever A is noncyclic or |S| >= 3; if A is cyclic and |S| >= 3 then |Jac| >= (3/2)^phi(n) n, and if the p-part of A is noncyclic then p^(2 + v_p(n)) divides |Jac|. The qualitative statement (Jac ~= A iff A cyclic and S = {a,-a}) is Benkart-Klivans-Reiner Proposition 6.19 (proof sketch due to S. Koplewitz), which answered V. Reiner's BIRS 2015 problem 1.9; this dossier gives an independent algebraic proof and the quantitative bounds.
resolves: none: the qualitative theorem is BKR Proposition 6.19 (arXiv:1601.06849v2); contributes an independent written proof and quantitative bounds (pending specialist review)
verified: check_cayley_jacobian.py: exhaustive Smith-normal-form check for |A| <= 12, |S| <= 4; product formula n|Jac| = prod lambda_chi; exact orbit-norm factorisation, p^2 divisibility and the AM-GM bound on cyclic groups n <= 12; cyclic-subgroup count exceeding the exponent for noncyclic p-groups of order <= 64; control without the sum-zero hypothesis.
cayley_jac.py: exhaustive scans (|A| <= 24, |S| <= 5: 32,551 cases; |A| <= 14, |S| <= 7: 19,633 cases): Jac ~= A only for cyclic {a, -a}.
check_bound.py (6,236 cases) and check_norms.py (1,601 cyclic cases, exact resultants): all proof ingredients hold.
unresolved: whether the quantitative bounds (|Jac| >= (3/2)^phi(n) n for cyclic A, s >= 3; p^(2+v_p(n)) | |Jac| for noncyclic A_p) are known
